extra.message: Insecure deserialization using pickle.loads() on untrusted user-supplied payload. An attacker can execute arbitrary commands on the server by supplying a malicious serialized object.
OS command injection via unsanitized user-supplied parameter 'host' directly concatenated into os.system() command. This allows arbitrary command execution.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) in Jinja2 template rendering. The user input 'fragment' is concatenated directly into Template structure, allowing arbitrary template code execution.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: XML External Entity (XXE) injection via lxml parser configured with resolve_entities=True and no_network=False. This enables attackers to retrieve local files, perform SSRF, or trigger denial of service.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: NoSQL Injection vulnerability. Untrusted structured JSON payload from body is passed directly to MongoClient's find_one() query, allowing query structure manipulation.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: Path Traversal vulnerability allowing arbitrary file write. User-controlled parameter 'ref' is concatenated to construct a file path under BASE_EXPORT_DIR without validation, enabling writing outside designated folder.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Neutralization of Input Across Multiple Path Levels

extra.message: Missing authentication and access controls for sensitive administrative view course_grade_file_096, exposing business internal contact details and payment flags publicly.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: Open Redirect vulnerability. View course_return_lane_163 redirects the browser to any external site specified in user parameter 'lane' without domain check.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: Permissive CORS policy. Origin header is reflected directly into Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header, while Access-Control-Allow-Credentials is set to true, leaking user data to foreign origins.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive CORS Policy with Credentials

extra.message: Improper certificate validation via ssl._create_unverified_context(). This bypasses certificate checks, leaving backend HTTPS communication open to MITM (Man-In-The-Middle) attacks.
Security Misconfiguration. Disabling security protective headers such as X-XSS-Protection and Content-Security-Policy leaves users vulnerable to browser-level scripting attacks.
Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) on state-changing view admin_user_toggle. Changing system state via GET request bypasses Django's CSRF protection.
Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) on state-changing view assignment_status. Allowing status change on GET requests exposes the functionality to unauthorized state modifications by third-party links.
Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) on state-changing view release_grade. Releasing student grades via GET makes it vulnerable to automated CSRF attacks.
Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) on state-changing view request_resubmission. Demanding submission resubmission via GET exposes grade status change to CSRF link execution.
Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) on state-changing view discussion_moderate. Moderate actions such as locking/pinning threads are triggered via GET and can be executed via CSRF.
